historicalMissingForRetiredGyanBinary.details: GyanD/codexffmpeg release 9.0.2 contains binaries and a FFmpeg upstream commit only; repository root contains .github and README.md, not the custom dependency build orchestration, patches or build dependency lock. Compiler provenance MSYS2 GCC 16.2.0 Rev3 does not establish that ordinary MSYS2 package recipes produced these binaries.
Exact configure enables all eight libraries, while publisher external-version list supplies no versions for them.

Primary release archive/tag attempts did not locate these exact versions. Cairo tag list has 1.18.4 and 1.18.6, so 1.18.5 is not uniquely identified by a release tag; publisher needs to identify development commit. libgme tag API showed 0.6.5 latest; 0.6.6 exact tag absent. Intel libva exact 2.25.0 tag absent at attempted endpoint. No replacement version was used.

No publisher link map, pkg-config --static closure, source/patch lock or per-library configuration provided. Additional static dependencies and their precise revisions/notices are not established (e.g. dependencies selected by Cairo/fontconfig/GnuTLS/FreeType/SDL/SRT/OpenMPT; these examples are not asserted as linked). GCC runtime/MinGW runtime provenance and applicable runtime exceptions also require identification.

Pinned complete MSYS2 MINGW-packages source archive includes standard PKGBUILDs and patches. These are expressly reference-only, not asserted to match Gyan. For example x264 recipe is r3222.b35605a versus binary r3223.0480cb0, x265 recipe 4.3 versus binary 4.3+45, Cairo recipe 1.18.6 versus publisher 1.18.5.

historicalPackagingInstructionsForRetire: Keep acquired archives intact; README members inside source archives may remain but must not be extracted or copied as standalone README files.

Runtime bundles include license texts, copyright notices and a compact version/source-origin summary only. Keep source archives, reference recipes and build evidence separately in the project materials; do not copy them into the application bundle.

Do not describe these materials as complete corresponding source, treat the gate as passed, or publish/redistribute the fixed binary until missing publisher materials and complete source/license closure are resolved.
